title: swarm
text: This creature is made up of countless smaller creatures.

title: Interception
text: When this creature is on guard and a ranged attack targets a non-flying object in the same zone, that creature may direct the ranged attack on itself, provided it is a legal target for that attack.

title: Training
text:
Your magician is trained in one or more schools of magic.
If you take a spell from a school in which your magician is not trained, you must pay spell points equal to twice the level of that spell.
Some spells belong to more than one school of magic.
Some spells belong to multiple schools and have an "&" symbol connecting those schools.
Some magicians are enemies of certain schools.
Example: The Beastmaster is trained in natural magic.
Since each spell can only be used once during the game, you'll want to have multiple copies of important spells.

title: Canceled, canceled
text: When a spell, attack, or effect is canceled or canceled, it stops and has no further effect.

title: Discard pile
text: Each magician has his own discard pile.

title: Activate
text: When you take an action phase with a creature, you activate it.

title: Struck
text: If a creature is pushed into a wall that was blocking the passage trait, it gains the battered trait.

title: Attack spells
text: Attack spells allow the user to attack a target in the arena.

title: attack
text: The #linked attack sequence table shows the different types of attacks in Mage Wars and their exact sequence.

title: Attack action
text:
An attack action is a quick or full creature action to make an attack.
Some attacks, such as counterstrike, wall attacks, or summons, do not consume their own action.

title: Attack on passage
text: Any creatures that move through such a wall are automatically attacked by that wall.

title: Onslaught +X
text: The creature gets +X attack dice for its immediate next melee attack if it makes that attack immediately after a move action in which it moved at least 1 zone.

title: Ethereal
text: This attack is magically enhanced.

title: Reveal costs
text:
When you reveal a face-down enchantment, you turn its card face-up.
You can reveal an enchantment immediately after any step, phase, or action in the game:
- at the end of any phase of the game round.
- immediately after a creature is activated, before it chooses its actions this turn.
- immediately after a creature completes an action, such as an attack, movement, or summoning a spell.
- at the end of each step of an attack, casting a spell, or moving.
- you can reveal an enchantment immediately after it is cast, right after the Cast Spell step.
- you may not interrupt an event to reveal an enchantment.

title: expansion
text: When you summon such a wall, you may pay an additional cost equal to the wall's mana cost and level when you cast the spell.

title: Wipe out
text: When you wipe out an object, it is permanently destroyed without a trace.

title: Equipment (spells)
text: Equip spells give your mage new or stronger abilities.

title: Evasive
text: Such a creature is fast and cunning.

title: Friends
text: A friendly object is one that is currently controlled by the player themselves, or (in multi-player games) by a player on their team.

title: Limited life
text: This creature cannot be healed, regenerate, or gain life.

title: Protected
text: This object is protected from enemy magic.

title: incantation (spell)
text: A summon spell summons an object into the arena that remains in play until destroyed.

title: Disposal costs
text: Most states have a removal cost, printed on the tile as a small black number in a gray dot.

title: Owner
text: The owner of a spell is the player who had that spell in their spellbook at the start of the game.

title: Stunned
text: The creature is incapacitated.

title: Moving summoning
type: Summons are attached to the zone they are in,
text: however, some incantations can move (like Raincloud).

title: Movement action
text:
During its action phase, a creature can take a move action that allows it to move from one zone to an adjacent zone.
STEP 1: Announce Movement - Choose the zone you want the creature to move to.
STEP 2: Pay Costs - You must pay any costs associated with the movement.
STEP 3: Zone Exit Effects - Any spells, abilities, or effects that trigger when a creature leaves a zone now take place.
STEP 4: Walls - The creature now encounters any walls in its path.
STEP 5: Movement - The creature must be moved to the new zone.
STEP 6: Zone Enter Effects - Any spells, abilities, or effects that trigger when a creature enters a zone now take place.
If a creature becomes unable to move during the move action, its movement stops at that exact moment and the remainder of the move action is forfeited.

title: Flash +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: Psychic +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: Light +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: Blocks Line of Sight (SL)
text: This wall blocks line of sight (SL).

title: Bloodthirsty +X
text: This creature is a fierce predator with a thirst for blood.

title: Bleeding
text: This creature has suffered a deep, bleeding wound.

title: Taunt (Skeelax's Taunt)
text: Skeelax is a special creature that taunts his enemies into attacking him.

title: Taunt
text: Some creatures can taunt their enemy into attacking them.

title: Direct damage
text: Damage the creature takes immediately.

title: Double whammy
text: This attack makes a second attack against the same target as part of the same attack action.

title: Triple strike (triple strike)
text: This attack makes two additional attacks against the same target as part of the same attack action.

title: Penetrate +X
text: This attack subtracts X from the target's armor when determining damage.

title: Passage blocked
text: Creatures are not allowed to move through this wall.

title: Effect dice
text: The 12-sided die (also: D12) is called the effect die;

title: Standalone
text: This equipment is attached to a creature and functions independently of the creature.

title: Restrict
text: A creature that begins its action phase in a zone with any enemy creature has its movement restricted and can only move 1 zone in its action phase (even if it has the Fast trait).

title: Unique
text: Each player may have a maximum of 1 copy of this object in play at a time.

title: Defrost
text: This is a feature of flame attacks.

title: Uproot X
text: This creature can pull its roots from the ground and move freely.

title: Epic
text: Only 1 copy of this spell can be in a magician's spellbook.

title: Successful
text: An attack is considered successful and a hit if it neither missed due to the Dizzy condition nor was avoided by a defense.

title: Grab hold
text: This attack can grab creatures and drag them into your zone.

title: Conservation +X
text: This object's controller pays X mana during each maintenance phase, not the affected creature's controller.

title: To reach
text: This melee attack can target and attack flying creatures in the same zone.

title: trap
text:
An enchantment that triggers when an enemy enters the zone.
Some enchantments have the Trap subtype.
The trap is triggered when an opposing creature enters the zone through a move action, push, or teleport.
The trap is executed immediately after the creature is placed in the zone.
You can place any number of traps in the same zone as long as they have different names.
If the trap spell (like other mandatory enchantments) is revealed by an effect or property other than when an opponent enters the zone, the trap is destroyed without effect.
Only opposing creatures can trigger a trap spell, and it must trigger immediately when the creature enters the zone.

title: Rot
text: This is a toxic condition.

title: Ranged attack
text: This attack can be used against targets within its shortest and farthest range, and when they are in line of sight.

title: Ranged Attack +X
text: This creature gets +X attack dice when making a ranged attack.

title: Stuck
text: This creature gains the restrained and immobile characteristics.

title: Put out fire
text: This attack puts out fire.

title: Fireproof
text: The object can never be set on fire.

title: Flames +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: Fly
text:
Flying creatures fly over the field and can only be reached with a long-range attack.
Non-flying creatures cannot make melee attacks against a flying creature unless they have the reach trait.
Creatures with the fly trait and those without the fly trait do not restrict each other's movement.
When a flying creature makes a melee attack against a non-flying creature, it loses the Flying trait until the end of the attack action and is affected by damage barriers and counterstrikes as normal (the flying creature must dive from the air to the ground to make the attack).
A creature cannot gain or lose the flying trait during an attack action.
A flying creature is affected by guards when it makes a melee attack, but only when it attacks a non-flying creature in the guard's zone.
A creature may ignore the minimum range of the attack when making a ranged attack against an object in the same zone if either the attacker or the defender (or both) have the fly trait.

title: Formula (spell)
text: Formula spells only have a short-term effect on the game.

title: Frost +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: Frozen
text: A creature with a Frozen token rolls one die less for non-spell attacks and becomes cumbersome.

title: Melt X
text: The object melts over time.

title: Counterattack
text:
If a creature is the defender on a melee attack, and it has a melee attack as a swift action with the counterstrike trait, it can use that attack against the attacker.
The defender can counterattack even if the attacker's attack was "unsuccessful".
A creature can make exactly one counterstrike against each creature that attacked it in melee (even if the attacker made more than one hit in the attack).
The counterstrike can only be a single quick action melee attack.
If the defender is destroyed by the attack, he cannot counterattack.
Example: The Darkfenne Hydra has an attack with the counterstrike trait.
A counterstrike follows the normal attack sequence, starting with Step 1: Declare Attack.

title: Opponent
text: Any enemy object currently controlled by an enemy player.

title: Smashed
text: The creature is incapacitated.

title: Curbed
text: If a creature has the restrained trait, it cannot take movement actions.

title: Poison +/-X
text: Some attacks have the poison trait.

title: Incapacitated
text: An incapacitated creature cannot perform any actions, including moving, attacking, guarding, using spells, or counterstriking.

title: cure
text:
Healing immediately removes a number of damage from the target.
Important: Only living creatures and summons can be healed or regenerated.

title: Summon
text: When you cast a creature spell, it is also called summoning a creature.

title: Ichthellid larva
text: A creature with these condition tokens has an ichthellid larva implanted into it.

title: Ignore
text: An ignored enemy creature cannot restrict the movement of friendly creatures.

title: Immune to poison
text: Non-living creatures are immune to poison.

title: Immune to Psychic
text: This object either has immensely powerful spiritual gifts or none at all.

title: immunity
text: This object is immune to all attacks, damage, conditions, and effects of the specified damage type, including critical damage and direct damage.

title: On fire
text: The object is burning.

title: Inactive
text: Inactive is a state that temporarily suspends the function of an object.

title: Indirect
text: The Line of Sight (SL) of this ranged attack is not blocked by walls.

title: initiative
text: Players take turns having the initiative, which is indicated by the Initiative tile.

title: Climb
text: The creature can take a special full action to climb over any physical wall and move into the adjacent zone.

title: Counterattack
text: A spell that is countered cannot be cast.

title: More controlling
text: All spells or objects in the game are controlled by the player who cast them.

title: Physically
text: Physical objects are normal, physical objects.

title: Disembodied
text: An insubstantial, amorphous object that is almost impervious to damage.

title: creature (spell)
text: Creature spells summon a creature to fight for you in the arena until it is destroyed.

title: Critical damage
text: Critical damage bypasses armor (this does not reduce damage taken).

title: Slow
text: This creature is very slow.

title: Life
text: Creatures and summons have a life attribute.

title: Life +/-X
text: The object gains or loses X lives.

title: Live
text: Living objects can be healed, regenerated, and given life.

title: Covenant of Life +X
text: During the maintenance phase, you may either shift X damage from your mage to this object or from this object to your mage, regardless of distance and line of sight (SL).

title: Lifelink +X
text: This is a mage trait that can be used in team games.

title: Legendary
text: Only 1 copy of this object may be in play at a time.

title: level
text: All spells have a level, which is printed as a small number next to that spell's school.

title: magician
text: This creature is a mage, and it represents the player in the game. The mage can gather mana, cast spells, and can perform a special quick cast action each round.

title: School
text:
There are six primary or "high" schools of magic: the Dark School
the spiritual school
the Holy School
the Arcane School
the nature school
the war school
There are also four elementary or “minor” schools:
Earth School
Air school
Water school
Fire school
The associated magicians are called fire magicians, war magicians, spiritual magicians, etc.

title: Mage Binding +X
text: Such an enchantment is not easily applicable to a magician.

title: Mana drain +X
text: If this attack deals damage to an opposing creature, the creature's controller loses X mana from their mana pool (if they have any).

title: Mana collection
text: Some objects have the Mana Gathering attribute.

title: Mana collection +/-X
text: Modifies a creature's mana collection attribute by +/- X. Mana collection can never fall below 0.

title: Mana Transfer +X
text: Just like Mana Drain +X, with the following addition: Whoever controls this attack gains mana equal to the mana lost.

title: marker
text: A marker is a small marking chip that is intended to remind you of certain things.

title: Multiple attack
text: Some attacks consist of multiple separate attacks against the same or different targets.

title: Melee +X
text: This creature gets +X attack dice when it makes a melee attack.

title: Melee attack
text: A close range attack that can only affect targets in the same zone.

title: Not alive
text: All non-living creatures have the traits Immune to Poison and a Limited Life.

title: Lesser creature
text: A level 1 or 2 creature. Differentiated from: Higher creature.

title: Higher creature
text: A creature of level 3 or higher.

title: Lesser magic
text: A level 1 or 2 spell. Differentiated from: Higher Spell.

title: Higher magic
text: A level 3 or higher spell.

title: novice
text: Basic apprentice spells.

title: Magic book
text:
When you create your spell book, you will spend your magician's spell points to purchase your desired spell cards.
If you want to put a spell from a school in which your mage was trained into your spellbook, you must pay spell points equal to that spell's level.
Some magicians are enemies of certain schools.
Since each spell can only be used once during the game, you'll want to have multiple copies of important spells.

title: Only for X mages
text: Some spells are restricted to certain mage classes.

title: Mage class
text: The magician class determines the skills of the magician played.

title: OR attacks
text: Some attacks have an OR in their attack bar.

title: Care of X
text: All attacks against this object have X fewer attack dice.

title: object
text: Enchantments, equipment, creatures, and summons are spells that become objects in play and that remain in play after they are cast.

title: Plague
text: A small, annoying creature that cannot hinder opponents.

title: Ready
text: The Ready tiles are used to indicate when traits have been used.

title: Tendrils
text: The vine tiles are living summons with life force 1, no armor, and they cannot receive armor.

title: Resuscitate
text: This creature is resurrected from death.

title: Regenerate X
text:
This object heals (takes away) X damage from itself during each maintenance phase.
Important: Only living creatures and summons can be healed or regenerated.

title: Reconstruct
text: Reconstruct is an effect that removes damage from nonliving creatures.

title: Saving throw
text: Some conditions and enchantments require a saving throw (using the effect die to determine whether they can be taken by the creature they are attached to.

title: Round punch
text: This attack occurs in a wide, sweeping arc and can target and hit 2 different targets in the same zone.

title: armor
text: During an attack, armor is subtracted from the normal damage of the attack dice.

title: Armor +/-X
text: Modifies an armor attribute by +/- X. Armor can never fall below 0.

title: Line of sight (SL)
text:
To cast a spell or make an attack, you must have uninterrupted vision of the target (line of sight or SL for short).
When determining the range, you also need to check whether you have a free SL.

title: Damage type (+/-X)
text:
Damage can be of a specific type.
Flame
Water
Light
flash
Poison
Supersensory
wind
frost
.
Same damage type modifiers are added together.

title: Damage barrier
text:
A damage barrier surrounds an object and performs an automatic attack against any enemy that melee attacks an object surrounded by such a barrier.
A damage barrier gives the defender a “free” auto attack against any defender who made a successful melee attack on them.
A damage barrier can attack each attacker once per round.
Note: A damage barrier only works against melee attacks.
Damage barriers work automatically and do not require an action to be used.
Important: Each object can only be protected by one damage barrier.

title: Sleep
text: This is a supernatural state.

title: Fast
text: This creature can take 2 move actions before taking a swift action.

title: Quick action
text:
In their action phase, creatures can take a move action followed by a swift action.
MORE MOTION ACTION
The acting creature moves 1 additional zone to an adjacent zone, according to normal movement rules.
PERFORM QUICK ATTACK
Your creature can make an attack from its card that has the Quick Action icon on it.
KEEP GUARD
The acting creature can choose to defend the zone it is in by keeping guard.
USE QUICK SPELL
A creature with the ability to cast spells (such as your mage or a familiar) can cast a spell that has the swift action symbol.
PERFORM SPECIAL QUICK ACTION
Some creatures have a special action they can perform.

title: Quick spell
text: A quick spell requires a quick action to cast. )on its effect bar, directly to the right of its casting cost.

title: Quick cast action
text:
Each magician can perform a special additional action per round, the quick cast action.
A quick cast action is a special action that only a mage may perform during a round, in addition to his normal actions during his action phase. ).
- In the introductory quick cast phase
- Immediately before or after any of the creatures under your control resolve their action phase
- In the final quick cast phase
When you use your quick cast action, you turn over your quick cast stone and cast a quick spell.

title: Quick cast phase
text: There is a quick cast phase at the beginning and end of each action level.

title: Weak
text: A poisonous condition that weakens a creature.

title: Clumsy
text: This creature is clumsy and/or limps.

title: Dwindling X
text: Objects with Fading X only last a short moment before disappearing.

title: Dizzy
text: The creature is disoriented and/or blinded.

title: Push
text: The Push effect is triggered by some spells and attacks that move the target to an adjacent zone.

title: Stumbling
text: Staggering is a condition that disorients or unbalances a creature.

title: Teleportation
text: An effect that moves an object directly to another zone, ignoring walls and objects.

title: Taunt (Thorg's Taunt)
text: Thorg, head of the bodyguard, can taunt his enemies.

title: Hit
text: When an attack reaches the Damage & Effects step, it counts as a hit relative to its target.

title: trick
text: Whenever this spell is destroyed or discarded, it is returned to its owner's spellbook instead of the discard pile.

title: Unstoppable
text: This Krature is exceptionally large, heavy and/or strong, possibly animated by powerful magic.

title: Immobile
text: The object cannot be pushed.

title: Untenable
text: This creature has a smooth and/or amorphous body, making it difficult to capture.

title: Unclean
text: This curse or poison attack causes an unclean or infected wound that will not heal.

title: Invisible
text: This object is invisible and cannot be targeted (there is no Line of Sight (SL) to this object).

title: Unavoidable
text: Defenses cannot be used to avoid the attack.

title: Indestructible
text: This object is incredibly resilient when it comes to damage.

title: Indestructible
text: This object cannot be damaged or destroyed by damage.

title: Original life +X
text: This creature's life force is higher than normal.

title: V’Tar
text: This is the raw, unaltered power of the Plane of Voltari.

title: V’Tar Orb
text:
The V'Tar Orbs are the key to powering the ancient V'Torrak artifact.
The balls are represented by double-sided markers.
The balls start the game “neutral” and no player controls them.
Orbs cannot be destroyed.

title: V’Torrak artifact
text:
This zone contains a long-standing V'Torrak artifact that can break the boundaries between worlds and provide its controller with near-infinite mana.
Note: If this zone part loses its special ability (perhaps because a terrain spell replaces its effect), the V'Torrak artifact is then considered "buried under this zone" and the player who collects enough V'Tar still wins the game.
Placement Tip: The V'Torrak works well if you place it near zones with V'Tar spheres.

title: Vampiric
text: When this attack deals damage to a living creature, the attacker heals (taking away damage) for half the damage dealt (rounding up).

title: Anchored
text: This object has an extraordinary connection to the astral plane of Etheria and resists any attempt to magically transport it.

title: Covert enchantment
text: All enchantments are applied face down and remain unrecognizable to your opponent.

title: Darkened
text: This object is difficult to see.

title: Prevention effects
text: Some spells can prevent an event if certain costs are not paid.

title: Taunt (Sosrukos' Taunt)
text: This is a special condition that can arise from the attack of certain creatures (in the base game: Sosruko, Ferret Familiar).

title: Crippled
text: This is a toxic condition.

title: Rusting
text: Rusting is an acidic condition that eats away armor.

title: Devour
text: This creature eats other creatures!

title: defender
text: A creature or summon that is being attacked.

title: defense
text:
Some objects have the Defense attribute, which represents the ability to avoid an attack.
The gold shield indicates the defense attribute.
Important: A creature may never use more than one defense against a single attack (even if it has multiple mandatory enchantments, all of which must be revealed when it is attacked)!

title: Confidant
text:
Familiars are creatures that can use spells.
If a familiar is under your control during the planning phase, you may choose one spell for each familiar to use during the round (in addition to the two spells for the mage).
When your familiar resolves its action phase, you can have it cast this spell.
The familiar is considered the caster of the spell for all rules purposes, including range, etc. The spells your familiar uses are under your control. If your familiar does not use its prepared spell, the spell goes back into your spellbook at the start of the next planning phase.

title: Rooted
text: This creature is firmly rooted in the ground.

title: enchantment (spell)
text: Enchantments are different from all other types of spells because they are played face down.

title: Complete action
text:
If a creature does not take a move action in its action phase, it may take a full action. ).
PERFORM FULL ATTACK
Your creature can use an attack from its card that has the full action symbol.
USE FULL SPELL
A creature with the ability to use spells (such as your mage or a familiar) can use a spell with the full action symbol.
PERFORM SPECIAL FULL ACTION
Some creatures have a special action they can perform.

title: Complete magic
text: A full spell requires a full action to cast. on its effect bar, just to the right of its casting cost.

title: Applied by the magician
text: This spell can only be used by a magician.

title: keep watch
text:
As a swift action, a creature can choose to stand guard to protect its zone and gain the counterstrike trait.
- Counter Strike: As long as the creature is on guard, all of its quick melee attacks have the Counter Strike trait.
- Protect Zone: If a creature is in a zone with one or more enemies standing guard, it may not make a melee attack against an object without a guard token.
Only melee attacks are affected.
Use guards
Keeping Guard allows you to protect important creatures or summons.
Remove guards
If a guard is the target of a melee attack, you must remove their guard tile as soon as the attack ends at the end of Step 8: Counter Strike - even if the attack did not hit.

title: Alert
text: This creature permanently guards, protects, and protects friendly objects.

title: Wall
text:
Ramparts are special types of incantations that are printed in landscape format.
Passage blocked
Attack on passage
Blocks Line of Sight (SL)
expansion
If the wall does not have the Attack on Passage or Passage Blocking symbol, creatures can simply move through it.
Attack walls
A creature in either zone adjacent to a wall may make a melee attack on that wall.

title: Water +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: Wind +/-X
text: A type of damage.

title: growth
text: A creature with the Growth condition token has increased in size.

title: Anger +X
text: If this creature is wounded, it reacts extremely wildly and aggressively.

title: Tough -X
text: This creature is tough and resists the effects of attacks.

title: Spellbind
text:
Spellbind is a feature possessed by some objects (most commonly equip spells).
When you cast a spell with the Spellbind trait, you immediately bind a spell to it.
Bound formulas or attack spells are not discarded after being cast.
Some spell binding items allow you to swap the bound spell for another.
Example: You can bind any formula to the magician's wand.

title: Magic source
text:
Objects with the Spell Source trait have the property that they can cast spells for you.
During the deployment phase, both players can cast these spells, starting with the player who has the initiative.
Most spell sources also have a mana gathering attribute, meaning they generate their own mana during the mana gathering phase.
Spell Sources apply spells the same way your mage does, using the card's target and range.
Example: The Beastmaster has a dwelling with mana collection 2. In each mana collection phase he places 2 mana tiles on the dwelling.

title: Destroyed
text: A destroyed object is removed from play and placed in its owner's discard pile.

title: zombie
text: This creature was resurrected from death.

title: Zone
text: A zone is a square region in the arena used for movement, object placement, and range determination.

title: Zone attack or zone spell
text:
This attack or spell affects all creatures and summons in the target zone without actually targeting them individually.
Zone attacks always target an entire zone, never an object.
In Step 3: Missed Roll, you roll a zone attack only once to see if it misses the zone;

title: Zone unique
text: There can never be more than 1 zone-unique summon in each zone.

title: Zone control
text: A player controls a zone if they control a creature in that zone and their opponent controls none.

title: Zone edge
text: The dividing line between two adjacent zones.

title: Condition and effect
text:
Objects can take on different states, indicated by tiles placed on the object.
An effect is a short, immediate change in the target's status.
A condition lasts longer and is marked with a tile on the target.
All states can also exist multiple times on the same object.
Most conditions can be removed in a specific way.
